author: Astrokillah
text:
Hi PinkPanter,

I only trade when I can babysit my position. Forex is designed to take
stops, I am not a superman like Master Traders here that can pin-pint
exact entry with 1 pip stop loss. I have given up trying to do that.

I normally trade when there is no red news. I'm a scalper, so when price
 ranges, it will either get to my TP or if it overshoot my 'mental
stop', it will always retrace and let me get out with some minor profit.
 And I like to enter a trade when I see existence of multiple barriers
behind my stop loss. Because I know even when my stop is hit, price will
 get to the next barrier and bounce back towards my entry, allowing me
to get out with minor loss. And more often than not, I split my
positions. So if my full risk is 5 lots, I will split them into 2x2.5
lots, I would enter with 2.5 lot first, if it goes into drawdown, I will
 add the other 2.5 at the next barrier. Most of the time, price would
bounce back towards my entry. This kind of trading can get ugly (so a
hard stop is required beyond the second position), but 90% of the time
it gives amazing return.

On one of my diagram above, I mentioned 'contrarian', this is crucial in
 my trading, it's about knowing where price wants to go (I call this
'juicy' level). Most of the time we focus so much on entry, but
contrarian is target-oriented, I can enter a trade without the best
entry, with a bigger stop loss than I normally use, but I feel good
about it, because I am 99% sure that price would get to where I think it
 will go. So before I take a trade, I need to ask myself, where is the
juiciest level I see on the chart? And where is a logical place for IT
to take stops before they go towards their target. If I see a juicy
level above current price, I would never short. Likewise, I will never
long if there is a juicy level below.

Lots of words, not sure if it helps. I guess what has really made a
difference in my trading is when I put my heart and soul into
understanding price movement on 1-min chart.

author: Astrokillah
text:
This is going to be a long post, as I have received several pm asking
 me how do I scalp, I thought I owe a lot to this community so I am
going to use this opportunity to give it back. Scalping is not hard, but
 it requires more screen hours per day. There are several rules I
follow:

Rule#1: NO RED NEWS

Rule#2: Understand how Pro Money work.

With regards to Rule#2, there is one paragraph, taken from "The Doctor's Patients" journal, that I hang on my wall:

Remember, for prices to rise they must first fall, why? Unless Pro
Money can get you stopped out, trading in the wrong direction, they will
 not have enough profit margin to start the move and make it pay.

I am going to use a scalp on GBPJPY as an example. Looking at the Weekly
 chart, it shows that we are now at a critical area where heavy tricks
were played in the past. I have no idea what price is going to do, so
entering and holding a trade hoping for 50RR is out of the question for
me.

But scalping is always available.. and is available 24/7. So I look at what price is doing on H4:

Two things to point out:

1) Note the messy area inside red circle. Conventional SD theory says
this is a low quality demand zone, because it's not clean, too many
candles. Well to me, this is utterly nonsense, because I often see such
messy zone acting as very strong support/resistance area. It's very
difficult for price to break such zone.

2) Look at how price bounced from the tip of that zone, this is classic
Pro Money at work, they used RED NEWS to drop the price hard, real hard,
 and made everyone think that the time has come, it's finally turning,
and they sold into the trap set up by Pro Money.

So looking at how price has been moving since it hit that blue
horizontal line, it broke higher high, and now is taking a breather,
that begs the question: do you think Pro-Money are done? Pro-Money
were already up there at 156.44 level, why did they drove price down and
 then drove it back up to the same level?

Next up is 5 min chart, just before I took a scalp. Looking at this, I made up my mind, I'm going to scalp long:

Then I look at 1-min chart and what I see:

The first thing that gave me confidence about taking a long is that
price has broken into CPAZ. This is actually one of the most powerful
concept introduced by Master IF: When a PCP is broken, price would
travel to the end of the CPAZ. So I smelled blood. The question is,
where do I entered? I saw price making a very nice ascending TL, I
remember Doctor's words of wisdom:"Price has to fall before it can rise". So naturally I set my BUY limit order below that dubious TL, and my TP just below the tip of the CPAZ.

And here were the outcome. Not sure if you can see the blue dotted line and the arrows, so I marked my entry/exit manually.

This little scalp pushed me over +62%:

At the moment, price is back to ranging again, it even went lower than
my exit point, so if I hold this trade hoping for bigger RR, I would
have gotten nothing out of it. Do I think Pro Money are done? No, I
don't know.. doesn't look like it. I would follow Doctor's medicine:

A safer way to trade is to wait a few days after the daily/weekly
turn has established a new direction because people have spent a life
time of fortune trying to pick tops and bottoms.

Until that happens, I shall happily remain in scalping mode.

This week has been good to me. Caught several big trades and I am near
 doubling my account. First was this USDCAD long that gave me 7R:

And now I totally regretted not holding it

But that's beside the point, now, I have learned to be contented.. not
letting missed opportunity affect my emotion, it's more important to me
to finish each day on a positive balance than aiming for high RR.

There is one aspect of trading that still haunt me, and it is to do with
 determining which flag is going to hold or fail, I have often observed
the following:

The above is a diagram when price is trending up, the same applies when
price is trending down. What I often noticed was, as price is trending
up, it tends to create staircase of flags along the way, it would then
hit a historical zone (a supply level to the left) and dropped towards
the flags. Sometimes, it would bounce at the first flag (A), but more
often than not, it would break the first flag but bounce from the second
 flag (B). I have been a victim of this many times in the past, because
each time, when I saw the first flag getting engulfed, I thought ok,
seems like it's ready to change direction, so I went short, but then
price gets to the next flag and rallied up strongly. So I have
recently made some adjustment to my trading plan, if I decide to touch
trade, I would enter a smaller lot size at the first flag, if it fails, I
 would enter a larger lot size at the second flag. If both flags fail,
then I would surrender and exit both trades.

The second big trade was taken on GBPJPY, at the First Engulf

See this following GBPJPY recent price action, it has shaken my faith (a

 little.

We look closer within the red circle area:

So as price rallying up, it created a CPAZ and FL-A. Price hit UFL, this
 is the 3rd test (as you can see from first chart above). Nevertheless,

 the UFL, it would be a valid short setup and we must put our stop loss
above the UFL.

author: Rinehart
text:
That is badass AK!!!! Your account growth is a thing of beauty but really the best part is your very, very low drawdown!

I want to give you a piece of advice although at this point you have
become the mentor and I'm going to be asking you questions, lol.

You are on fire right now (the last few months actually). At some point
 in the future, the market will change it's personality, e.g. moving
from consolidating markets to trending markets, low volatility to high
volatility, etc. Sometimes when this happens a trader who was in tune
with the market suddenly falls out of sync. You go from a high batting
average to struggling. Often when this happens the trader will trying
to study harder, analyze their losing trades, make tweaks and changes,
trying to get back to killing it in the market. This is actually very
dangerous and counter productive. If one is not careful they can lose
sight of what was making them very successful especially once the market
 goes back to behaving in a way that suits the trader.

What I recommend is you go back through your last 50 trades and analyze
them right now while you are still "seeing" the market. Write down what
 type of trades you took, what type of SL placement, how did you manage
the trades (partial profit at TG1, full profit at TG2). Because this
information will be invaluable one day when you fall out of sync with
the market.

author: Astrokillah
text:
Thank you Rinehart, I could never thank you enough for your help.
Since I joined this community, you have always been watching over my
shoulder!

I managed to tripled my account, took 33 trading days (since January 2).

From the equity curve, you can see that I'm a scalper, and honestly, I'm
 not proud of it, because I much prefer to set and forget. I have tried
catching big RR trades but with limited success so far and my impatient
steered me towards the easy path - scalping. So I am determined to fix
this. I am going to stop scalping for a month and only focusing on
taking quality trades: LSK, SRK, First Engulf, First Kink.

Scalping on 1 min may not be for everyone, but it's actually not as
daunting as most people wants you to believe. The most important thing
is to make sure that you have HTF zone in control. And by HTF zone I
mean H4 and above. Start your analysis from Monthly, Weekly, Daily and
H4. Make sure you know where the key levels are. For example, price is
dropping fast, and it eventually hit H4 demand, watch on LTF what price
is doing, when you see bullish engulfing candles, followed by price
making higher-low, higher-low - that's bullish signs. But more
importantly, look at big picture, price do not travel in straight line,
even though the overall picture is bearish, price loves to retrace
upward to shake out weaker hands, look to see if there's a juicy H4
supply above where ITs can use to take stops before dropping the price
majorly again. When all the above conditions are met, now you pay
attention to LTF supplies, these are supplies created when price was
dropping hard, and when you see price engulfing north of a LTF supply,
it's giving you a sign that it's ready to move towards the next LTF
supply. Wait for price to retrace, take long entry at LTF demand,
target next LTF supply.

Sorry, it's too much words, It's time for me to fix my addiction to
scalping. Probably I should stop trading live, go back to demo again and
 only trade set and forget.

author: Astrokillah
text:
Frosty, scalping needs fast decision making, so you have no time to
calculate your lot size! Also, you need to make sure that there is NO
RED NEWS. I cannot emphasize this enough. NO RED NEWS, NO RED NEWS.

I use a fixed lot size when I scalp.. between 1 lots to 5 lots to start,
 depending on how confident I was on the particular setup. I can even go
 20 lots if I am 200% sure that the target is going to be hit.

Throw RR out of the window. When I scalped, I look for the absolute
amount of money, so it's how many dollars am I getting out of each
scalp, and it's not about RR. Sometimes I would take profit for $100
(if I see my scalp is going nowhere after sometimes but I'm still in
profit). Scalping is best when price is ranging.

I said I 'started' with 1 lots (to 5 lots), because I would double up my
 position in case my first zone fail. Refer to the diagram I posted on
post #262. If my first zone fail, I would enter again the lower demand
zone with 2 x first position size. And I would exit both trades when
price return to my first entry. You have to have the discipline to get
out when both zones fail..
